title: Create your mba.com account
detail: Register for the free Official Starter Kit and use your name exactly as it appears on your passport.

title: Read the roadmap lesson
detail: Read From GMAT to Admit and jot down which of the three paths feels most like you.

title: Start your wins file
detail: Create one document with a line per work achievement: date, what you did, the number, who noticed.

title: Check your passport
detail: Confirm validity and that your name matches your degree certificates. Start renewal if needed.

title: Read the ISB class profile
detail: Open ISB's official class profile and note the experience, women percentage and GMAT range. Write what surprised you.

title: Map experience rules
detail: For ISB, LBS MiM, Imperial and HEC, write the exact experience rule and how many months you will have on that date. Check the official site.

title: Read the global programmes lesson
detail: Note which programmes cap experience near two years and which flex to three.

title: Choose a work project to own
detail: Ask your manager to let you own one project from start to finish. Agree how you will measure results.

title: Ask about your MOI certificate
detail: Contact Jesus and Mary College and Delhi University offices about a Medium of Instruction certificate and transcripts. Ask for the process in writing.

title: Set up your Admissions tracker
detail: Add your first 8 to 10 programmes to the tracker with the experience rule and a source for each number.

title: Read the funding lesson
detail: Sketch a rough budget for ISB and one European programme. Mark every figure as official or third-party.

title: Update the wins file
detail: Add this quarter's results with numbers. Note one result you could use in an essay.

title: Pick a quant or analytics course
detail: Choose one statistics, accounting or analytics course to finish by June. Add it to your calendar.

title: Attend an info session
detail: Join one online info session for a shortlisted school and write down one detail that surprised you.

title: Talk to a current student or alumna
detail: Message one student or alumna from a target programme. Ask what they wish they had known.

title: Cut your list to 4-7 programmes
detail: Sort into reach, target and safe. Write one honest sentence on why each one fits you.

title: Check scholarship pages
detail: List scholarship names, eligibility and deadlines for each shortlisted school. Include Forte where the school participates.

title: Draft your why-now paragraph
detail: Write five sentences on why management and why now: evidence, gap, plan. It is a first draft only.

title: Scan your documents
detail: Scan mark sheets, degree or provisional certificate and ID. Store them in one folder per school.

title: Plan your recommender conversations
detail: Decide who you will ask and what examples you want them to remember. Do not write their letter.

title: Book your GMAT
detail: Book the exam for Saturday 28 August 2027, about 7 weeks ahead. Check that your ID name matches.

title: Draft your resume
detail: Rewrite each bullet with action, scope and metric. Keep it to one page.

title: Brief your recommenders
detail: Send the recommender pack: goals summary, resume, examples, deadlines. Offer a 20-minute chat.

title: GMAT first attempt
detail: Saturday. Sleep well, arrive early, bring valid ID. Plan a quiet day afterwards.

title: Debrief the GMAT
detail: Write down what went well and what did not. Decide whether the October backup is needed.

title: Check the official ISB deadline
detail: Open isb.edu and confirm the Round 1 and Round 2 dates and the opening of applications. Update the tracker.

title: Draft your goals essay
detail: Write the short-term goal, long-term goal, gap and bridge. Keep it rough.

title: Check early-round dates for experience-capped programmes
detail: Confirm LBS MiM and Imperial rounds, and recount your months of experience on each school's date.

title: Write why-this-school drafts
detail: For each target, add two specific features, one person you spoke to, and what you would contribute.

title: GMAT backup attempt (if needed)
detail: Mid-October window. Only sit it if your first score is below your target and you have a plan to improve.

title: Write a STAR story bank
detail: Draft three STAR stories: leadership, failure, influence. Use true numbers.

title: Send recommender reminders
detail: Check that each recommender has the link and the deadline. Offer help, not pressure.

title: Practise the 25 interview questions
detail: Record yourself answering five questions on your phone. Watch for filler words.

title: Final polish before Round 2
detail: Read essays aloud, proofread, and check every school's name. Submit a few days early.

title: Practise video answers
detail: Do five 60-second answers with a timer, using the answer, evidence, link shape.

title: Mock interview with a friend
detail: Do a 30-minute mock interview and ask for specific feedback.

title: Check scholarship deadlines
detail: Confirm scholarship cut-offs for each school, including any March dates. Apply where required.

title: Compare loan options
detail: Collect terms from at least three lenders: rate, moratorium, fees, collateral. Do not sign anything yet.

title: Check the experience date
detail: Confirm your months of experience on 31 March 2028 and make sure your forms state them accurately.

title: Research JN Tata and other funds
detail: Check the official JN Tata timeline and eligibility. Note deadlines in your tracker.

title: Compare offers
detail: Build a simple scoring table: outcomes, cost, fit, network, life, risk. Talk to two students per offer.

title: Handle waitlists
detail: Follow each school's waitlist instructions. Send one strong update only if allowed.

title: Accept an offer and pay the deposit
detail: Read the deposit terms and deadline. Withdraw from other schools politely.

title: Start visa and loan paperwork
detail: Open the official government and school pages for visa steps. Request loan sanction letters.

title: Plan pre-programme prep
detail: Make a short plan: quant refresh, finance basics, reading list. Thank your recommenders.
